inputs.original_text: This is being called “chaos,” but what stands out is a huge “No Kings” protest met with tear gas and arrests by federal officers. At least 13 arrests were confirmed in Portland and Denver. Labeling protesters “agitators” shifts attention away from the power imbalance: the state has force at its disposal, while people exercising their right to dissent face intimidation and arrest. A society that protects democratic rights should safeguard protest, not treat mass dissent as a threat to be suppressed.
inputs.modified_text: Calling this “chaos” obscures what happened: a huge “No Kings” protest was met with tear gas and arrests by federal officers, with at least 13 arrests confirmed in Portland and Denver. Branding demonstrators “agitators” is a familiar way to delegitimize dissent and shield state power from scrutiny. When people protesting face intimidation and arrest while the state commands force, that is a serious threat to democratic rights. Protecting those rights means safeguarding protest, not suppressing it.
